item.title: Iran’s Protests Have Ended, but the Anger and Pain Haven’t
item.description: In the aftermath of another wave of antigovernment unrest, Iran is gripped by a mood of collective grief and uncertainty about the future.

item.title: Dana Eden, Co-Creator of ‘Tehran,’ Dies During Filming of Fourth Season
item.description: Ms. Eden, 52, who was also an executive producer of the Emmy-winning show, was found in a hotel room in Athens. Greek police said they did not suspect foul play.

item.title: Cortina’s 70-Year-Old Curling Stadium Is a Star at the Winter Olympics
item.description: It hosted the 1956 Olympics and had a role in a James Bond movie. Now Cortina’s beloved stadium is packed with raucous fans, and the occasional cheating scandal, in curling.

item.title: Syrian Army Crosses New Threshold With Advances in Kurdish Regions
item.description: The advance of the Syrian Army into Kurdish regions could put nearly all the country under one authority. But it ends a dream of autonomy for ethnic Kurds.

item.title: A Russian ‘Village of Military Valor’ Waits for Its Reward
item.description: A provincial governor seeks to honor villages that deployed many soldiers to the war in Ukraine with a prestigious title first bestowed on cities that were major World War II battlefields.

item.title: Prices Jump as Venezuelans Abroad Consider Buying Property Back Home
item.description: Nicolás Maduro’s capture and talk of oil investment have pushed prices higher, even as brokers say enthusiasm is outpacing demand in a weak economy.

item.title: Who’s Pulling the Strings on the World Stage? Ask the Puppets.
item.description: Eurasia Group, the geopolitical risk consultancy run by Ian Bremmer, gets into the political satire game with its Instagram show “Puppet Regime.”

item.title: In Xi Jinping’s Purge of the Military, a Search for Absolute Loyalty
item.description: By reaching back to Maoist tactics of “rectification,” the Chinese leader is signaling that control over the gun requires a state of perpetual cleansing.

item.title: New Research Absolves the Woman Blamed for a Dynasty’s Ruin
item.description: A Chinese king’s infatuation with a woman was seen as the reason that a golden age collapsed. Evidence suggests climate change and internal strife played bigger roles.

item.title: Gisèle Pelicot Speaks
item.description: She was repeatedly drugged by her husband and raped in a series of crimes that shocked the world. Pelicot talked to us about her new memoir.

item.title: Iran Protester Dies in Custody, Raising Fears of Execution
item.description: Rights groups are investigating the death of Ali Rahbar as a potential extrajudicial killing. Iran denies executions have taken place.

item.title: Canada Gives U.S. Arms Makers the Cold Shoulder on Military Spending
item.description: Canada plans to unveil a new strategy that will shift its current reliance on American companies to Canadian military suppliers.

item.title: U.S. Deports Nine Migrants in Secret, Ignoring Legal Protections
item.description: Most had court orders protecting them from removal to their home countries, so they were sent to detention in Cameroon.

item.title: Europe Today Looks Different From the One Trump’s Team Describes
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio appealed to European leaders in Munich by stressing Christian and cultural bonds that are no longer universal.

item.title: Three American Speeches at Munich, and Plenty of Confusion
item.description: As the U.S. message veered from shared heritage and values to shared interests and back again, Europeans wondered what kind of alliance they were left with.

item.title: How Bangladesh Went From Revolution to Elections
item.description: Bangladesh held the first national elections since a student revolution in the summer of 2024. Standing outside the Dhaka university, the epicenter of the student movement, New York Times correspondent Anupreeta Das explains what the recent elections mean for the country’s future.

item.title: How Italy’s Federica Brignone Won Gold in Giant Slalom.
item.description: At 35, Federica Brignone of Italy became the oldest Olympic Alpine gold medalist. Mikaela Shiffrin of the U.S. finished a disappointing 11th.

item.title: Islamist Party’s Rise Overshadows Student Revolution in Bangladesh
item.description: The party is dedicated to running the country under Islamic law, but ran on a more moderate platform. It gained far more seats in last week’s election than it ever had before.

item.title: You’d Be Surprised to See Where Many Olympians Keep Their Medals
item.description: Athletes train and sweat for years in pursuit of the glittering prizes. Many store them in the least glamorous places.

item.title: Trump’s Stinging Attack on Israel’s President Touches a Nerve
item.description: President Trump called President Isaac Herzog of Israel “disgraceful” because he has not yet pardoned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his corruption trial.

item.title: French Prosecutors to Investigate Diplomat as Part of Epstein Probe
item.description: The Paris prosecutor’s office said it was looking into three new complaints with links to the files and revisiting an earlier investigation into an Epstein associate who died in 2022.

item.title: No miracle, but Denmark hockey team gives U.S. a good fight.
item.description: The Americans trailed Denmark after one period, but fought back to cruise to a 6-3 victory.

item.title: Europe’s Reaction to Rubio: Relief, Up to a Point
item.description: The secretary of state was much less caustic in Munich than Vice President JD Vance was a year ago. But European officials said his core message was much the same.

item.title: Milo Rau’s ‘Hate Radio,’ ‘Pelicot Trial’ and More Theater of the Real
item.description: Milo Rau’s examination of the infamous broadcast that preceded the Rwandan genocide is onstage now. Two other works, including “The Pelicot Trial,” arrive in March.

item.title: Lucas Pinheiro Braathen of Brazil and Mikhail Shaidorov of Kazakhstan Win Olympic Gold Medals
item.description: A Brazilian skier secured South America’s maiden medal at a Winter Games the day after a Kazakh figure skater won his nation’s first winter gold in 32 years.

item.title: Gisèle Pelicot, the Woman at the Center of Rape Trial That Shook France, Shares Her Story
item.description: In her first interview with an American media outlet, Pelicot opens up about surviving years of secret abuse — and a trial that shocked the world.

item.title: Will A.I. Kill Translation Jobs?
item.description: Popular paperbacks are being translated with the help of machines, raising anxiety among professionals in the field.

item.title: How $40-a-Pack Cigarettes Pushed Australians to the Black Market
item.description: Tax hikes made cigarettes in Australia the most expensive in the world. They have also helped fuel a multibillion-dollar criminal enterprise in bootleg tobacco.

item.title: In Munich, Rubio Stresses Shared History to Europeans but Warns of ‘Civilizational Erasure’
item.description: In his speech at the Munich Security Conference, Secretary of State Marco Rubio voiced some far-right ideas, but his diplomatic tone came as a relief to the audience.

item.title: Thousands Rally for Iran Regime Change in Cities Around the World
item.description: People protesting the Iranian government gathered near the security conference in Munich, as well as in other cities. More U.S.-Iran talks are expected Tuesday.

item.title: Scotty James Is Edged Out by Yuto Totsuka of Japan in the Halfpipe.
item.description: Scotty James of Australia laid down a strong run, but was outdone by Japan’s Yuto Totsuka.

item.title: Navalny Was Poisoned With Frog Toxin, European Governments Say
item.description: The toxin was found in the body of the Russian dissident Aleksei A. Navalny, who died in prison two years ago, five governments said, challenging Russia’s official account.

item.title: In Munich, Europe Says It Is ‘De-risking’ From the U.S. Amid Trump’s Unpredictability
item.description: In Munich, European leaders were also talking about “de-risking” from the United States, citing President Trump’s unpredictability.

item.title: Here’s the latest.
Pakistan Accused of Denying Treatment for Imran Khan’s Failing Eyesight
item.description: The lawyer for the former prime minister claimed he had lost 85 percent of the vision in his right eye because of delayed treatment in prison.

item.title: After Mass Shooting, the Town of Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia Is Forever Changed
item.description: The mass shooting in the remote British Columbia mining town has shocked and saddened the nation.

item.title: The Sea Took Her Prosthetic Leg. Months Later, It Gave It Back.
item.description: Brenda Ogden lost her waterproof prosthetic leg 10 months ago, and with it, her zest for swimming. Then a local fossil hunter stumbled upon it.

item.title: Open Road
item.description: On Valentine’s Day, consider the ways in which we’re sticking to established paths — and the places where we yearn to deviate.

item.title: Roy Medvedev, Soviet Era Historian and Dissident, Is Dead at 100
item.description: His score of books and hundreds of essays documented Stalinist executions, Communist repressions and censorship, and the transition to post-Soviet Russia.

item.title: Zelensky rules out holding elections until there is a cease-fire with Russia.
Amid Fallout From Epstein Files, Dubai’s DP World Boss Is Replaced
item.description: Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem was credited with turning DP World into a global logistics powerhouse. He was recently identified in correspondence with Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Brazil, the World’s Largest Catholic Nation, Embraces Polyamory
item.description: More people in a still largely conservative and religious nation are rejecting monogamy as they seek new definitions of romance, and of family.

item.title: Japan Releases Chinese Boat Captain After Detaining Him for 30 Hours
item.description: The captain’s arrest had raised fears of a broader diplomatic confrontation between Japan and China, which have been at odds for months.

item.title: Life in Beirut Beneath the Drones
item.description: More than a year into a cease-fire, the mechanical whir of Israeli drones above the Lebanese capital is a reminder that, in many ways, the war never really ended.

item.title: First U.S. Troops Land in Nigeria for Trump-Led Christian Mission
item.description: The deployment follows months of escalating pressure from President Trump on the African nation, including a surprise missile strike on Christmas Day.

item.title: How Peter Biar Ajak, a Sudanese Peace Activist, Was Caught Plotting a Coup
item.description: Peter Biar Ajak, a democracy advocate, was convicted of conspiring to buy and export weapons for a revolt in South Sudan.

item.title: Ilia Malinin’s catastrophic free skate: ‘I blew it.’
item.description: Malinin, the heavy favorite to win gold, fell twice during his final routine and finished 8th.

item.title: As Diplomats Talk, Pentagon Prepares for Possible War With Iran
item.description: President Trump threatened to strike Iran, but the military has needed time to build up its forces in the region.

item.title: Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ Said to Have Raised First Pledges for Gaza
item.description: The United Arab Emirates and the United States have each committed more than $1 billion to President Trump’s new international initiative, officials said.

item.title: The Mutually Beneficial Ties Between Jeffrey Epstein and Thorbjorn Jagland
item.description: Thorbjorn Jagland, a former prime minister of Norway who led the Nobel Committee, promised influence, and the disgraced financier had gifts to give, new emails show.

item.title: At Munich Summit, European Leaders Agree With Trump: The Old World Order Is Over
item.description: At the Munich Security Conference, U.S. officials softened their tone but not their message: Europe should pay its own way. European leaders increasingly agree.

item.title: U.N. Condemns U.S. Measures Halting Oil Deliveries to Cuba
item.description: The measures were installed last month by the Trump administration after the U.S. captured Nicolás Maduro and seized control of Venezuela’s oil industry.

item.title: Germany’s leader says his country is in discussions with France on a European nuclear deterrent.
Macron urges Europe to step up on the global stage and stresses unity on major issues, particularly Ukraine.
Key Moments in Gisèle Pelicot’s Interview With The New York Times
item.description: The woman at the center of France’s largest-ever mass-rape trial told us about her life before, during and after the abuse she suffered at the hands of her husband.

item.title: Can’t Buy Love? Kenya Bans Bouquets Made of Cash.
item.description: Floral arrangements crafted from carefully-folded, colorful bank notes, had become a popular symbol of love in Nairobi.
